explanation: A polynomial's far-left and far-right behavior is decided entirely by its leading term a·x^n. The degree n controls whether the two ends agree: even n makes both arms point the same way, odd n sends them opposite ways. The sign of a flips everything — positive a lifts the right end, negative a turns the whole picture upside down. Step n through whole numbers and watch the colored end-arrows snap to match the even/odd rule.
bullets: Even n: both ends point the SAME way; odd n: ends OPPOSE.
a > 0 lifts the right end up; a < 0 reflects the whole graph.
Only the leading term a·x^n matters for the far-left/far-right ends.
